_meta.title: Network-Level Attacks
_meta.description: Position and interception: spoofing, poisoning, hijacking, and the routing-tier moves that shift entire traffic flows. Maximum blast radius class - anything that redirects traffic is gated to explicit operator confirmation.

techniques.name: ARP Spoofing / MITM Positioning
techniques.summary: Flood gratuitous ARP replies mapping the gateway's IP to your MAC; hosts send their traffic to you first. Combined with port mirroring or SSL stripping it becomes full credential capture. Purely local-segment scope, trivially detected, still effective on unmanaged networks.

detection.description: MAC-flapping on switch ports (same MAC bouncing across ports), gratuitous-ARP rate anomalies, duplicate IP alarms, gateway IP resolving to non-gateway MAC in host caches; DHCP starvation usually accompanies it.
mitigations: Dynamic ARP Inspection + DHCP snooping on switches (the actual fix)
Static ARP entries for critical infrastructure pairs
802.1X to keep rogue devices off the segment
TLS everywhere - MITM position without TLS stripping is mostly metadata

techniques.name: DNS Poisoning & Spoofing
techniques.summary: Inject forged DNS responses: on-path guessing with transaction-ID prediction (Kaminsky-class cache poisoning), rogue DHCP DNS assignment, or local hosts manipulation. Redirects everything downstream - which is why DNSSEC and port randomization exist.

detection.description: Resolver analytics: unusual response source ports/addresses, TTL anomalies on popular records, NXDOMAIN bursts (subdomain enumeration is noisy in the same logs), organic lookup volume to unregistered domains via a single host.
mitigations: DNSSEC validation on resolvers
Source-port + query-ID randomization (modern resolvers have it; audit old ones)
Split-horizon hygiene: internal resolvers forward only to trusted upstreams
Monitor for DHCP options 6 changes

techniques.name: TCP Session Hijacking & RST Attacks
techniques.summary: On-path sequence-number tracking lets you inject into an established stream (desync then command injection) or send forged RSTs to kill connections (IDS evasion, VoIP/long-session disruption). Mostly a LAN or compromised-router technique in modern practice.

detection.description: TCP retransmission/ACK anomalies per flow (IDES-class heuristics), unexpected RST storms between specific pairs, session resumption from different source IPs, out-of-window segment counters on stateful devices.
mitigations: Encrypted, integrity-checked sessions (TLS 1.3) - injected bytes die at the MAC check
TCP-AO for routing/infrastructure sessions
Stateful inspection devices flag out-of-window traffic

techniques.name: BGP Hijacking & Route Manipulation
techniques.summary: Announce prefixes you don't own (origin hijack) or a more-specific path (path poisoning) to attract traffic for interception or blackout. Nation-state tier: nation-states and large ASes have executed it for interception (documented incidents exist). Affects the whole internet's view, not one network.

detection.description: Route monitoring (RIPE RIS, RouteViews) for origin/AS-path anomalies on your prefixes, sudden geolocation shifts of inbound source, RPKI-invalid announcements, certificate pinning failures reported by clients (passive DNS + RPKI dashboards are the operational answer).
mitigations: RPKI ROA publication for every prefix (origin validation)
ASPA (path validation) as it deploys, max-prefix limits with peers
IRR + RPKI hygiene, IRR filtering discipline on your edge
Certificate pinning in clients for crown-jewel apps (interception becomes visible)

techniques.name: LLMNR/NBT-NS/mDNS Poisoning (Responder-class)
techniques.summary: Answer Windows name-resolution fallback queries (typo'd hostnames, WPAD lookups) claiming to be anything, capturing NetNTLMv1/v2 hashes from the victims. The classic first 20 minutes of an internal engagement - capture, crack offline, or relay upstream (welds directly to the NTLM relay technique).

detection.description: Multiple hosts answering LLMNR/NBT-NS queries (legitimate: zero extra responders), WPAD resolution anomalies, EID 4625/4776 auth bursts to a single host after name queries, RDP/HTTP auth attempts to hosts with no service.
mitigations: Disable LLMNR/NBT-NS via GPO (the actual fix; no legitimate modern need)
Disable WPAD; DNS globally suffices
SMB signing everywhere (blocks the relay half)
Network IDS signatures for responder traffic patterns

techniques.name: Host & Service Discovery (Network Scanning)
techniques.summary: The first move of nearly every real engagement: ICMP sweeps, ARP discovery on the local segment, SYN/connect scans for listening services, version fingerprints to pick targets. Read-class by nature - but scanning is NOT harmless: known-naive connect scans have hard-crashed printers, OT/ICS gear, and fragile legacy services, so scope and rate discipline are operational safety, not courtesy. Outside the engagement scope a scan is indistinguishable from pre-attack recon, which is the whole reason defenders instrument for it.

detection.description: Shape, not signature: one source touching many ports on one host, or many hosts on one port - both are scan shapes visible in Zeek/Suricata scan detectors and firewall deny spikes; Windows sides show EID 5156 connect-storm patterns; honeypot canaries (unused RFC1918 space, decoy services) give certain-signal alerts; sudden DNS/ARP sweep traffic marks host-discovery phases; asset-inventory diffs flag services that appear where none were.
mitigations: Deny-by-default east-west segmentation - shrink what any scan can even see
Canary nets and decoy hosts on every segment; any touch is a high-fidelity alert
NAC (802.1X) so only managed endpoints get a routable identity
Baseline inventory + anomaly alerting on new listening services
